title: Last Stop on the Route
statement:
You get a list of one-way legs legs, where legs[i] = [from, to] means a trip goes directly from city from to city to. Together the legs form one route through distinct cities with no loops and no branches, but they are given in any order.

Return the name of the city where the route ends: the one city that no leg leaves from.

examples.why: The route is Seoul → Daejeon → Busan → Daegu. Every city but Daegu has a leg leaving it.
One leg: it ends at y.
The last leg in the list is not the last leg of the route. Taking the "to" of the final entry gives m, which is wrong.

constraints: City names are 1–10 letters or digits
The legs form a single path with no repeated city
hints: What is special about the final city compared with every other city on the route?
Every city except the last one appears as a "from" exactly once. The last one never does.
Put all "from" cities in a set, then find the "to" city that is not in it.

explain.intuition:
Think in terms of out-degree: how many legs leave a city. On a single route every city has one leg leaving it, except the last city, which has none. So the answer is the only to city that never appears as a from.

Checking that by scanning all legs for every candidate is O(n²). A hash set of all from cities makes each check O(1): build the set in one pass, then scan the to cities until one is missing from it.
steps: Add every from city to a set leaves.
Scan the legs again and look at each to city.
Return the first to city that is not in leaves.
pitfalls: Returning the to of the last entry in the list. Legs come in any order.
Looking for the city that appears only once across all legs. The first city of the route also appears once, as a from.

solutions.title: Check each destination against every leg
solutions.idea: For each "to" city, scan all legs to see whether any leg leaves from it.

solutions.title: Set of departure cities
solutions.idea: Every city except the last has a leg leaving it. Collect the departures and find the destination that is not among them.

followups: Return the whole route in order, from first city to last.
The legs may form several separate routes. Return every end city.
